raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fix the root cause of #31624: ModelOpt Llama-4 (Scout/Maverick FP8) checkpoints take 68s-495s to load depending on hardware, dominated by H2D copies from non-contiguous CPU tensors.

These checkpoints store expert weights fused as `[num_experts, hidden_in, hidden_out]`. `Llama4Model.load_moe_expert_weights` transposes to the runtime orientation with a stride-only view, so `RoutedExperts._load_w13`/`_load_w2` end up calling `expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)` with a non-contiguous CPU source. ATen materializes `src.contiguous()` on the CPU first, and for fp8 that gather has no vectorized path, so it costs 3-4s per expert tensor. That is where the load time goes.

Per https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31624#issuecomment-3706297841, the fix should keep the CPU weights contiguous rather than move checkpoint tensors to the GPU. This PR does that by flipping the strided side of the copy to the destination:

```python
expert_data.transpose(-1, -2).copy_(loaded_weight.transpose(-1, -2))
```

`loaded_weight.transpose(-1, -2)` undoes the earlier view and recovers the contiguous on-disk slab at zero cost, so the H2D transfer is dense. The layout transform runs as a strided device-side write into the existing parameter storage. No copy of `loaded_weight` is retained in GPU memory at any point; ATen's transient staging buffer is allocator-managed inside the copy op. TP-narrowed slabs (unit inner stride, padded row pitch) degrade to host row-run memcpys instead of an elementwise gather and then take the same dense path. That is the case that defeated the shard-first experiment in the issue thread.

Implemented as one helper (`_copy_h2d_dst_strided`) applied at the three expert-weight copy sites in `routed_experts.py`. Contiguous sources are unaffected (byte-identical behavior). Since the fix lives in the fused-MoE loader rather than `llama4.py`, it applies to any model whose checkpoints arrive transposed.

Prior attempts on the issue, for context:

| Approach | Load time | Status |
|---|---:|---|
| Baseline | 68-78s | |
| Full-tensor CPU `.contiguous()` | 88s | worse than baseline |
| Final-slice CPU `.contiguous()` (#32081) | ~60s | independently benchmarked; #46766 takes the same approach |
| GPU-first transpose | 23-37s | rejected over GPU memory lifecycle |

This PR targets the 23-37s class without moving checkpoint tensors to the GPU.

## Test Plan

- `pytest -s -v tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_h2d_copy.py` (new): layout equivalence against plain `copy_` for contiguous, transposed, and TP-narrowed sources, strided destination views, dtype casts, and scalar fallbacks. fp8 and bf16 on CUDA, with a CPU-only subset.
- Microbenchmark of the three copy patterns before/after.
- End-to-end load time of `nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8` (`--quantization modelopt --kv-cache-dtype fp8`) before/after.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 18 passed (A100 80GB, CUDA fp8/bf16/fp32 + CPU subset):

```
$ pytest tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_h2d_copy.py -q
18 passed in 6.33s
```

Per-copy microbenchmark, A100 80GB PCIe (driver 560.35.05, torch 2.11.0+cu128), Scout-class expert slab shapes, best of 5:

| shape | dtype | baseline | #32081-style | this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (5120, 8192) | fp8_e4m3 | 62.8 ms | 62.7 ms | 4.0 ms | 15.8x |
| (5120, 16384) | fp8_e4m3 | 130.7 ms | 131.1 ms | 8.0 ms | 16.3x |
| (8192, 5120) | fp8_e4m3 | 63.5 ms | 64.3 ms | 4.1 ms | 15.5x |
| (5120, 8192) | bf16 | 93.4 ms | 93.6 ms | 7.5 ms | 12.4x |
| (5120, 16384) | bf16 | 194.5 ms | 196.2 ms | 15.9 ms | 12.2x |
| (8192, 5120) | bf16 | 95.4 ms | 96.1 ms | 7.5 ms | 12.7x |

TP-narrowed variants (row-run memcpy path): 1.0-1.5x. Peak CUDA memory during the benchmark: 320 MiB (transient, allocator-managed). Note the #32081-style per-copy numbers match baseline. Its e2e gain came from slicing before the gather, not from removing it.

E2E: the full Scout FP8 checkpoint (~110GB) doesn't fit one A100-80G, so this is a 24-layer truncation of `nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8` (57.35 GiB loaded, identical per-layer load path), warm page cache, 3 runs each. The modelopt capability gate (min 8.9) was bypassed for load-path measurement only; loading completes before any fp8 kernel selection.

| `Loading weights took` | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | mean |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main @ 576bf75d0 | 18.45s | 19.22s | 18.81s | 18.8s |
| this PR | 12.40s | 11.71s | 13.48s | 12.5s |

33% faster weight loading on this setup. The host here is a 2x EPYC 7763 (fast CPU gather); on the H200/Blackwell setups in #31624 where the gather costs 3-4s per tensor, the expected end-to-end gain is larger. **Update (2026-09-04):** @eric1932 ran the full untruncated 48-layer `nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8` on 1x H200, source-hash-verified builds, paired baseline/PR runs in separate processes, page cache confirmed 100% resident both sides:

| Version | 3 runs (s) | Median (s) |
|---|---|---:|
| Baseline @ 576bf75 | 104.46, 102.58, 101.87 | 102.58 |
| This PR @ 561b5bf | 23.63, 23.35, 24.33 | 23.63 |

4.34x, full model, on the H200 class this needed. Output tokens matched across all six runs. Thanks, full details below.

Note: built with an AI-assisted engineering workflow (Claude) under my direction, disclosed per the contributing guide: I specified the approach, reviewed each iteration, and validated the benchmarks. Co-authored-by trailer on the commit.

FIX #31624

Adding a full-model replication on **1× H200**: median weight-loading time dropped from **102.58 s to 23.63 s (~4.34× speedup)**.

**Setup**

- `nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8`: all 48 layers, including vision/projector weights; no layer truncation or CPU offload.
- PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.6.13` with its matching precompiled cache, 8 OMP/MKL threads.
- TP=1, ModelOpt FP8 weights, BF16 working dtype, FP8 KV cache, `max_model_len=2048`, `max_num_seqs=1`, eager mode.

**Comparison**

Both variants used the same baseline vLLM wheel and dependencies. Only `routed_experts.py` was switched between the parent commit `576bf75` and PR head `561b5bf`, with source-hash verification.

After one excluded baseline warmup, I ran three pairs in separate processes: baseline→PR, PR→baseline, baseline→PR. Model-file page-cache residency was 100% in the before/after snapshots for every run; this is not a continuous I/O measurement. No profiler was enabled for these timings.

| Version | Three runs (s) | Median (s) |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 104.46, 102.58, 101.87 | 102.58 |
| PR | 23.63, 23.35, 24.33 | 23.63 |

The metric is vLLM's `Loading weights took` log, not total startup or inference time.

The PR's 18 tests passed without skips. All six full-model runs completed a short greedy-generation smoke test with identical output token IDs. This does not establish model-quality equivalence, particularly with the uncalibrated FP8-scale warnings in this configuration.

The runner and raw logs are saved and available to share if useful. Thanks for the fix!

*Codex assisted with the test harness, execution, and analysis.*

Thanks for this. Full 48-layer model, H200 instead of my A100, source-hash-verified builds, paired runs to control for page cache. That's more rigor than I could add myself. 4.34x tracks with the microbenchmark: the CPU gather this removes doesn't get cheaper on newer GPUs, so it's a bigger share of the total on H200.

The uncalibrated FP8-scale warnings are a pre-existing property of this checkpoint, unrelated to this PR. Identical output tokens across all six runs confirms correctness, not calibration quality.

I'll add these numbers to the PR description with credit, and posted the same summary on #31624 so the two people planning to start don't duplicate a full model run.

This has been open since July 3 and is still conflict-free, but `pre-run-check` has never let CI run on it. That check needs a `ready` or `verified` label, or 4+ merged PRs by the author in this repo, and I have 0 here. No change to the PR can clear it.

Could a maintainer add `ready` so the test suite actually runs against it?

Where it stands:

- @eric1932 independently replicated it on 1x H200 with the full untruncated 48-layer `nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8`, source-hash-verified builds and paired runs: median `Loading weights took` 102.58s to 23.63s, 4.34x, identical output token IDs across all six runs.
- The approach is the one @robertgshaw2-redhat suggested on #31624, keeping the CPU weights contiguous rather than moving checkpoint tensors to the GPU. Undoing the transpose recovers the contiguous on-disk slab for free, so the H2D transfer is dense with no CPU-side gather and the layout change happens as a strided device-side write.
- 18 unit tests covering contiguous, transposed, and TP-narrowed layouts across fp8/bf16/fp32.
- It sits in `routed_experts.py` rather than `llama4.py`, so it covers any fused-MoE checkpoint that arrives transposed.

Two smaller PRs for the same issue are also open, #46766 and #50227, both the `.contiguous()` one-liner in `llama4.py`. If a maintainer prefers that route, that is a fine outcome and I would rather see #31624 closed than this merged. But right now none of the three can be evaluated on test results.

For context on the gate specifically, I have 3 merged in vllm-project/compressed-tensors and 1 in llm-compressor, which do not count toward the vllm threshold.

Rebased onto main. The conflict was with #54699, which landed in `_load_w2` a few hours ago, so it is worth spelling out how it resolved rather than just saying "rebased".

#54699 added a bounded write for a strided destination:

```python
if (loaded_weight CPU and expert_data CUDA and not expert_data.is_contiguous() and ndim == 2):
    loaded_weight = loaded_weight.contiguous()
    # chunked row copies, to cap the device temporary
```

That keys on the **destination** being strided. This PR keys on the **source** being strided. They are not the same condition, and both can hold at once, which matters because this PR deliberately moves the stridedness onto the destination. That is precisely the pattern #54699 exists to bound. So taking either side alone would have been wrong: dropping theirs regresses a memory bugfix, dropping mine keeps the CPU gather.

Resolved by composing them. The chunked write is now `_copy_h2d_bounded`, and every path through `_copy_h2d_dst_strided` routes its destination write through it:

| source | path | CPU gather | destination write |
|---|---|---|---|
| transposed view | undo transpose | none | bounded |
| TP-narrowed | row-run contiguate | row-runs, not elementwise | bounded |
| doubly strided | unavoidable gather | elementwise | bounded |
| already dense | passthrough, the #54699 case | none | bounded |

So #54699's guarantee holds on all four, including the two this PR adds, and the CPU gather is still removed in the case the issue is about.

Two notes:

- I did not extend this to the bias load at the bottom of `weight_loader`. It is 1-D, so neither `ndim >= 2` here nor `ndim == 2` in #54699 applies, and biases are small enough that neither rationale does either. Left deliberately.
- Tests: added a strided-destination parametrization across all three source layouts and a direct test that `_copy_h2d_bounded` splits a strided write and passes a contiguous one through. Verified byte-identical to `dst.copy_(src)` for all eight source/destination-layout combinations, and that a 17 MB strided write becomes 16 chunks of about 1.05 MB rather than one 17 MB staging buffer. `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean.

What I have **not** verified is peak device memory on real hardware, because `pre-run-check` still has not let CI run on this and I do not have a GPU attached at the moment. My original description said no extra device memory is *retained*, which is about retention rather than peak, and #54699 is specifically about peak. If a maintainer adds `ready` I would rather the runner settle that than keep asserting it.

cc @yuchenwang3 since this touches your change.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @ishrith-gowda.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Rebased onto main again (bf3d59052). The conflict was only textual, `_index_expert_mapping` from #58720 landing next to these helpers. Two fixes came out of re-reviewing it:

**1. A broadcasting `copy_` could raise.** `_copy_h2d_bounded` chunks both sides along dim 0, which assumes matching shapes. `_narrow_expert_data_for_padding` only narrows the hidden and shard dims when the destination is larger, and tolerates a lower-rank source, so equal shapes are not guaranteed. With a broadcast source big enough to need more than one chunk, the chunk lists differ in length and `zip(..., strict=True)` raises where plain `copy_` works. It now chunks only when shapes match and leaves broadcasting to a single `copy_`. Per-expert scales are small enough that this should not have triggered in practice, but it is a latent crash on a loader path. Note that #54699's original chunk loop, which has no `strict`, would instead silently write only the first chunk in the same situation.

**2. One of my tests had never actually run.** `test_bounded_copy_splits_strided_writes` asserted the write splits, but its tensor was 0.5 MiB, so it took one chunk and the assertion would have failed the first time CI ran this file. It now uses 2 MiB and counts the `copy_` calls issued, so forcing a single copy fails it. Chunking does not change the result, only peak device memory, so counting calls is the only way a CPU test can see it.

Test file: 15 passed, 11 CUDA-only skipped, locally. Mutation checked: dropping the shape guard and forcing the single-copy path each fail a test. `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean.

Still unmeasured, same as before: peak device memory on real hardware. That needs the GPU runner, which `pre-run-check` still has not let this PR reach.

Thanks for this PR — the dst-side flip is the right fix for #31624, and the
byte-identical contract (uint8-view comparison to defeat fp8 NaN equality) plus
the broadcast-chunk test give me good confidence. A few concrete points from a
line-by-line pass on top of current main:

**1. Bounded chunking can exceed the 1 MiB bound when rows are few.**
`_copy_h2d_bounded` computes `num_chunks = cdiv(src.nbytes, _H2D_CHUNK_BYTES)`,
but `torch.chunk(..., dim=0)` cannot produce more chunks than rows. For a
strided dst with e.g. 2 rows × 2 MiB, `cdiv` says 4 while `chunk` yields 2, so
each staged temporary is 2 MiB rather than the documented ~1 MiB bound. Real
MoE slabs have hundreds of rows so this is theoretical today, but the clamp is
one line:

```python
num_chunks = min(max(cdiv(src.nbytes, _H2D_CHUNK_BYTES), 1), dst.shape[0] or 1)
```

**2. Coverage gap: the "neither orientation is dense" fall-through is untested.**
The three tested layouts (contiguous / transposed / tp_narrowed) all route to
the first two branches. `_copy_h2d_dst_strided`'s last-resort path
(`src.contiguous()` + bounded dst write) is only reachable with a non-unit
inner stride, e.g. `base.transpose(-1, -2).narrow(1, 0, 16)`. Adding that as a
fourth `layout` in `_make_src` would pin down the fallback's correctness too.

**3. Fourth copy site intentionally left as plain `copy_`?**
`routed_experts.py:815` (the `w2` bias path in the expert-bias branch) still
uses `expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)`. I believe that's fine — expert biases
are 1-D/small so the helper's `ndim >= 2` guard would fall straight through —
but worth a one-line comment in the PR description so future readers don't
read it as an oversight.

**4. Datapoint request for the TP>1 row-run path.**
The `stride(-1) == 1` branch (TP-narrowed slabs) still pays a row-run memcpy
on the host; @jadechip's 2.2x B200 datapoint was TP=2, while the per-copy
microbenchmarks are TP=1. A sentence in the PR body on expected gain for
TP>1 (where the row-run branch is the hot path) would set expectations
correctly for operators.

Also confirming the PR applies cleanly on current main: the `_load_w2` inline
block it removes matches main byte-for-byte, and `cdiv` is already imported,
so no rebase obstacles from the last month of main.

Nice work — the generalization to `routed_experts.py` (any transposed fused-MoE
checkpoint, not just Llama-4/ModelOpt) is what makes this the fix #31624
needs, rather than another `.contiguous()` patch.

— Joseph (@JosephYouNew), reviewed on behalf of nothing but my own curiosity;
happy to help test or benchmark follow-ups.

Thanks for preserving the bounded-write path from #54699, and thanks @JosephYouNew for the review. I checked the chunk sizes and source strides on CPU.

The few-row case does exceed 1 MiB per copy, but clamping the chunk count to the row count leaves that unchanged: two 2 MiB rows still produce two 2 MiB copies. A strict byte bound would need tiling within a row, or the description could qualify the bound as row-granular.

For the fallback test, `base.transpose(-1, -2).narrow(1, 0, 16)` still takes the row-run branch: transposing it back leaves `stride(-1) == 1`. A genuinely doubly-strided view such as `base[::2, ::2].T` reaches the gather fallback.

I agree that documenting the 1-D bias exclusion would help. I haven't measured GPU peak memory or TP>1 loading on this revision, so I don't have updated numbers for those yet.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,180 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for _copy_h2d_dst_strided in routed_experts.py.
+
+The helper must be a drop-in replacement for ``dst.copy_(src)`` for every
+source layout produced by fused-MoE checkpoint loading (see issue #31624):
+contiguous slabs, transpose views of memory-mapped tensors, and TP-narrowed
+transpose views with unit inner stride.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.routed_experts import (
+    _H2D_CHUNK_BYTES,
+    _copy_h2d_bounded,
+    _copy_h2d_dst_strided,
+)
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv
+
+CUDA_DTYPES = [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16, torch.float8_e4m3fn]
+CPU_DTYPES = [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16]
+
+
+def _same_bytes(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    """Byte-level equality: a copy must reproduce the source exactly,
+    and this stays true for dtypes whose NaNs defeat torch.equal."""
+    return torch.equal(
+        a.cpu().contiguous().view(torch.uint8),
+        b.cpu().contiguous().view(torch.uint8),
+    )
+
+
+def _make_src(layout: str, dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Build a source tensor mimicking checkpoint loading layouts."""
+    # Disk layout of one fused expert slab: [hidden_in, hidden_out].
+    # Keep values within fp8_e4m3 range (max 448): out-of-range casts
+    # saturate to NaN, and NaN != NaN breaks torch.equal even for
+    # byte-identical copies.
+    base = (
+        (torch.arange(48 * 32, dtype=torch.float32) % 448.0).reshape(48, 32).to(dtype)
+    )
+    if layout == "contiguous":
+        return base
+    if layout == "transposed":
+        # Runtime orientation view, as created by llama4.py.
+        return base.transpose(-1, -2)
+    if layout == "tp_narrowed":
+        # Transpose view narrowed along the sharded dim (TP>1): unit inner
+        # stride with a padded row pitch.
+        return base.transpose(-1, -2).narrow(0, 8, 16)
+    raise ValueError(layout)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["contiguous", "transposed", "tp_narrowed"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", CPU_DTYPES)
+def test_same_device_matches_plain_copy(layout: str, dtype: torch.dtype):
+    src = _make_src(layout, dtype)
+    expected = torch.empty_like(src)
+    expected.copy_(src)
+    actual = torch.empty_like(src)
+    _copy_h2d_dst_strided(actual, src)
+    assert _same_bytes(actual, expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["contiguous", "transposed", "tp_narrowed"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", CUDA_DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
+def test_h2d_matches_plain_copy(layout: str, dtype: torch.dtype):
+    src = _make_src(layout, dtype)
+    expected = torch.empty(src.shape, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    expected.copy_(src)
+    actual = torch.empty(src.shape, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    _copy_h2d_dst_strided(actual, src)
+    assert _same_bytes(actual, expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
+def test_h2d_strided_dst_view():
+    """The destination may itself be a narrow of the parameter tensor."""
+    src = _make_src("transposed", torch.float32)
+    param = torch.zeros(64, 48, device="cuda")
+    dst = param.narrow(0, 8, 32).narrow(1, 0, 48)
+    expected = param.clone().narrow(0, 8, 32).narrow(1, 0, 48)
+    expected.copy_(src)
+    _copy_h2d_dst_strided(dst, src)
+    assert _same_bytes(dst, expected)
+
+
+def test_scalar_and_1d_fallback():
+    scalar_src = torch.tensor(3.5)
+    scalar_dst = torch.empty(())
+    _copy_h2d_dst_strided(scalar_dst, scalar_src)
+    assert scalar_dst.item() == pytest.approx(3.5)
+
+    vec_src = torch.arange(8, dtype=torch.float32)[::2]
+    vec_dst = torch.empty(4)
+    _copy_h2d_dst_strided(vec_dst, vec_src)
+    assert torch.equal(vec_dst, vec_src.contiguous())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
+def test_h2d_dtype_conversion():
+    """copy_ semantics include implicit dtype casts; the flip must too."""
+    src = _make_src("transposed", torch.float32)
+    expected = torch.empty(src.shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    expected.copy_(src)
+    actual = torch.empty(src.shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    _copy_h2d_dst_strided(actual, src)
+    assert _same_bytes(actual, expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["contiguous", "transposed", "tp_narrowed"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", CPU_DTYPES)
+def test_strided_destination_matches_plain_copy(layout: str, dtype: torch.dtype):
+    """A strided destination must still land byte-identical.
+
+    #54699 bounds the device-side temporary for a strided destination by
+    chunking the write. Flipping the strided side to the destination puts every
+    layout through that path, so each one is checked against a plain copy_.
+    """
+    src = _make_src(layout, dtype)
+    # same shape as src but non-contiguous, standing in for a padded TP view
+    expected = torch.empty(src.shape[::-1], dtype=dtype).transpose(0, 1)
+    expected.copy_(src)
+    actual = torch.empty(src.shape[::-1], dtype=dtype).transpose(0, 1)
+    _copy_h2d_dst_strided(actual, src)
+    assert _same_bytes(actual, expected)
+
+
+def test_bounded_copy_splits_strided_writes(monkeypatch):
+    """`_copy_h2d_bounded` chunks a strided destination and passes through a
+    contiguous one, and is byte-exact either way."""
+    # 2 MiB of float32, so the strided write actually takes the chunked path
+    src = torch.arange(512 * 1024, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(512, 1024)
+    assert cdiv(src.nbytes, _H2D_CHUNK_BYTES) > 1
+
+    contiguous_dst = torch.empty_like(src)
+    _copy_h2d_bounded(contiguous_dst, src)
+    assert torch.equal(contiguous_dst, src)
+
+    strided_dst = torch.empty(1024, 512).transpose(0, 1)
+    assert not strided_dst.is_contiguous()
+
+    # Chunking only changes how many copies are issued, not the result, so
+    # count them: a strided write of N chunks must be N copies, not one.
+    calls = []
+    real_copy = torch.Tensor.copy_
+
+    def counting_copy(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        calls.append(self.shape)
+        return real_copy(self, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.Tensor, "copy_", counting_copy)
+    _copy_h2d_bounded(strided_dst, src)
+    monkeypatch.undo()
+
+    assert len(calls) == cdiv(src.nbytes, _H2D_CHUNK_BYTES)
+    assert torch.equal(strided_dst, src)
+
+
+def test_bounded_copy_preserves_broadcasting():
+    """A broadcasting copy_ must stay a single copy_.
+
+    Chunking both sides along dim 0 assumes matching shapes. When ``src`` is
+    broadcast into ``dst`` it has fewer rows, so the chunk lists differ in
+    length: with ``strict=True`` that raises, and without it only the first
+    chunk would be written. The source here is large enough to need several
+    chunks, which is what exposes it.
+    """
+    cols = cdiv(_H2D_CHUNK_BYTES, 4) + 1024  # > 1 MiB of float32 per row
+    src = torch.arange(cols, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(1, cols)
+    assert cdiv(src.nbytes, _H2D_CHUNK_BYTES) > 1
+
+    expected = torch.empty(cols, 4).transpose(0, 1)
+    expected.copy_(src)
+    actual = torch.empty(cols, 4).transpose(0, 1)
+    assert not actual.is_contiguous()
+    _copy_h2d_bounded(actual, src)
+    assert torch.equal(actual, expected)

@@ -58,6 +58,72 @@ def _index_expert_mapping(
     return mapping_by_expert
 
 
+# A single copy_ into a strided CUDA destination can allocate a device-side
+# temporary covering the whole view, so strided writes are split into chunks of
+# about this many bytes. Introduced by #54699.
+_H2D_CHUNK_BYTES = 1 << 20
+
+
+def _copy_h2d_bounded(dst: torch.Tensor, src: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    """Copy a dense CPU ``src`` into ``dst``, bounding any device temporary.
+
+    When ``dst`` is a strided view, such as a padded TP slice, a single
+    ``copy_`` can stage the entire view on the device at once. Splitting along
+    the outermost dimension caps that staging buffer instead.
+    """
+    if dst.is_contiguous() or dst.shape != src.shape:
+        # A contiguous destination needs no bound. A shape mismatch means copy_
+        # is broadcasting, which chunking both sides along dim 0 cannot express,
+        # so leave that to a single copy_.
+        dst.copy_(src)
+        return
+
+    num_chunks = max(cdiv(src.nbytes, _H2D_CHUNK_BYTES), 1)
+    for dst_chunk, src_chunk in zip(
+        dst.chunk(num_chunks, dim=0), src.chunk(num_chunks, dim=0), strict=True
+    ):
+        dst_chunk.copy_(src_chunk)
+
+
+def _copy_h2d_dst_strided(dst: torch.Tensor, src: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    """Copy src into dst, keeping the host->device memcpy contiguous.
+
+    Fused-MoE checkpoints (e.g. ModelOpt Llama-4) store expert weights
+    transposed relative to the runtime layout, so ``src`` arrives here as
+    a non-contiguous CPU view of the memory-mapped checkpoint tensor.
+    ``dst.copy_(src)`` then materializes ``src.contiguous()`` on the CPU,
+    an elementwise strided gather that costs seconds per expert tensor
+    (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31624).
+
+    Flipping the strided side to the destination keeps the H2D transfer
+    dense: ``src.transpose(-1, -2)`` recovers the contiguous on-disk slab
+    at zero cost. That leaves the destination strided, which is the case
+    #54699 bounds, so the write goes through ``_copy_h2d_bounded`` rather
+    than a single ``copy_``.
+    """
+    if dst.device != src.device and src.device.type == "cpu" and src.ndim >= 2:
+        if not src.is_contiguous():
+            src_t = src.transpose(-1, -2)
+            if src_t.is_contiguous():
+                _copy_h2d_bounded(dst.transpose(-1, -2), src_t)
+                return
+            if src_t.stride(-1) == 1:
+                # TP-narrowed slab: unit inner stride but padded row pitch.
+                # Contiguation here degrades to row-run memcpys instead of an
+                # elementwise gather, after which the H2D transfer is dense.
+                _copy_h2d_bounded(dst.transpose(-1, -2), src_t.contiguous())
+                return
+            # Neither orientation is dense. Fall through: the gather is
+            # unavoidable, but keep the destination write bounded.
+            _copy_h2d_bounded(dst, src.contiguous())
+            return
+        # src is already dense; dst may still be a padded view.
+        _copy_h2d_bounded(dst, src)
+        return
+
+    dst.copy_(src)
+
+

     TENSOR = "tensor"
     CHANNEL = "channel"
@@ -428,7 +494,7 @@ def _load_per_channel_weight_scale(

-            expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)

-            loaded_weight.device.type == "cpu"

-            and expert_data.ndim == 2
-        ):
-            # A strided CPU-to-CUDA copy can allocate a full-shard CUDA
-            # temporary. Make the TP slice contiguous on CPU and copy rows

-            loaded_weight = loaded_weight.contiguous()
-            num_chunks = max(cdiv(loaded_weight.nbytes, 1 << 20), 1)

-                loaded_weight.chunk(num_chunks, dim=0),
-            ):
-                dst.copy_(src)

Adding a full-model replication on **1× H200**: median weight-loading time dropped from **102.58 s to 23.63 s (~4.34× speedup)**.

**Setup**

- `nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8`: all 48 layers, including vision/projector weights; no layer truncation or CPU offload.
- PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.6.13` with its matching precompiled cache, 8 OMP/MKL threads.
- TP=1, ModelOpt FP8 weights, BF16 working dtype, FP8 KV cache, `max_model_len=2048`, `max_num_seqs=1`, eager mode.

**Comparison**

Both variants used the same baseline vLLM wheel and dependencies. Only `routed_experts.py` was switched between the parent commit `576bf75` and PR head `561b5bf`, with source-hash verification.

After one excluded baseline warmup, I ran three pairs in separate processes: baseline→PR, PR→baseline, baseline→PR. Model-file page-cache residency was 100% in the before/after snapshots for every run; this is not a continuous I/O measurement. No profiler was enabled for these timings.

| Version | Three runs (s) | Median (s) |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 104.46, 102.58, 101.87 | 102.58 |
| PR | 23.63, 23.35, 24.33 | 23.63 |

- The approach is the one @robertgshaw2-redhat suggested on #31624, keeping the CPU weights contiguous rather than moving checkpoint tensors to the GPU. Undoing the transpose recovers the contiguous on-disk slab for free, so the H2D transfer is dense with no CPU-side gather and the layout change happens as a strided device-side write.

Two smaller PRs for the same issue are also open, #46766 and #50227, both the `.contiguous()` one-liner in `llama4.py`. If a maintainer prefers that route, that is a fine outcome and I would rather see #31624 closed than this merged. But right now none of the three can be evaluated on test results.

For context on the gate specifically, I have 3 merged in vllm-project/compressed-tensors and 1 in llm-compressor, which do not count toward the vllm threshold.

Rebased onto main. The conflict was with #54699, which landed in `_load_w2` a few hours ago, so it is worth spelling out how it resolved rather than just saying "rebased".

#54699 added a bounded write for a strided destination:

```python
if (loaded_weight CPU and expert_data CUDA and not expert_data.is_contiguous() and ndim == 2):
    loaded_weight = loaded_weight.contiguous()
    # chunked row copies, to cap the device temporary
```

That keys on the **destination** being strided. This PR keys on the **source** being strided. They are not the same condition, and both can hold at once, which matters because this PR deliberately moves the stridedness onto the destination. That is precisely the pattern #54699 exists to bound. So taking either side alone would have been wrong: dropping theirs regresses a memory bugfix, dropping mine keeps the CPU gather.

Resolved by composing them. The chunked write is now `_copy_h2d_bounded`, and every path through `_copy_h2d_dst_strided` routes its destination write through it:

| source | path | CPU gather | destination write |
|---|---|---|---|
| transposed view | undo transpose | none | bounded |
| TP-narrowed | row-run contiguate | row-runs, not elementwise | bounded |
| doubly strided | unavoidable gather | elementwise | bounded |
| already dense | passthrough, the #54699 case | none | bounded |

So #54699's guarantee holds on all four, including the two this PR adds, and the CPU gather is still removed in the case the issue is about.

Two notes:

- I did not extend this to the bias load at the bottom of `weight_loader`. It is 1-D, so neither `ndim >= 2` here nor `ndim == 2` in #54699 applies, and biases are small enough that neither rationale does either. Left deliberately.
- Tests: added a strided-destination parametrization across all three source layouts and a direct test that `_copy_h2d_bounded` splits a strided write and passes a contiguous one through. Verified byte-identical to `dst.copy_(src)` for all eight source/destination-layout combinations, and that a 17 MB strided write becomes 16 chunks of about 1.05 MB rather than one 17 MB staging buffer. `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean.

What I have **not** verified is peak device memory on real hardware, because `pre-run-check` still has not let CI run on this and I do not have a GPU attached at the moment. My original description said no extra device memory is *retained*, which is about retention rather than peak, and #54699 is specifically about peak. If a maintainer adds `ready` I would rather the runner settle that than keep asserting it.

cc @yuchenwang3 since this touches your change.

merged. Please rebase the PR, @ishrith-gowda.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Rebased onto main again (bf3d59052). The conflict was only textual, `_index_expert_mapping` from #58720 landing next to these helpers. Two fixes came out of re-reviewing it:

**1. A broadcasting `copy_` could raise.** `_copy_h2d_bounded` chunks both sides along dim 0, which assumes matching shapes. `_narrow_expert_data_for_padding` only narrows the hidden and shard dims when the destination is larger, and tolerates a lower-rank source, so equal shapes are not guaranteed. With a broadcast source big enough to need more than one chunk, the chunk lists differ in length and `zip(..., strict=True)` raises where plain `copy_` works. It now chunks only when shapes match and leaves broadcasting to a single `copy_`. Per-expert scales are small enough that this should not have triggered in practice, but it is a latent crash on a loader path. Note that #54699's original chunk loop, which has no `strict`, would instead silently write only the first chunk in the same situation.

**2. One of my tests had never actually run.** `test_bounded_copy_splits_strided_writes` asserted the write splits, but its tensor was 0.5 MiB, so it took one chunk and the assertion would have failed the first time CI ran this file. It now uses 2 MiB and counts the `copy_` calls issued, so forcing a single copy fails it. Chunking does not change the result, only peak device memory, so counting calls is the only way a CPU test can see it.

Test file: 15 passed, 11 CUDA-only skipped, locally. Mutation checked: dropping the shape guard and forcing the single-copy path each fail a test. `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean.

Still unmeasured, same as before: peak device memory on real hardware. That needs the GPU runner, which `pre-run-check` still has not let this PR reach.

Thanks for this PR — the dst-side flip is the right fix for #31624, and the
byte-identical contract (uint8-view comparison to defeat fp8 NaN equality) plus
the broadcast-chunk test give me good confidence. A few concrete points from a
line-by-line pass on top of current main:

**1. Bounded chunking can exceed the 1 MiB bound when rows are few.**
`_copy_h2d_bounded` computes `num_chunks = cdiv(src.nbytes, _H2D_CHUNK_BYTES)`,
but `torch.chunk(..., dim=0)` cannot produce more chunks than rows. For a
strided dst with e.g. 2 rows × 2 MiB, `cdiv` says 4 while `chunk` yields 2, so
each staged temporary is 2 MiB rather than the documented ~1 MiB bound. Real
MoE slabs have hundreds of rows so this is theoretical today, but the clamp is
one line:

```python
num_chunks = min(max(cdiv(src.nbytes, _H2D_CHUNK_BYTES), 1), dst.shape[0] or 1)
```

**2. Coverage gap: the "neither orientation is dense" fall-through is untested.**
The three tested layouts (contiguous / transposed / tp_narrowed) all route to
the first two branches. `_copy_h2d_dst_strided`'s last-resort path
(`src.contiguous()` + bounded dst write) is only reachable with a non-unit
inner stride, e.g. `base.transpose(-1, -2).narrow(1, 0, 16)`. Adding that as a
fourth `layout` in `_make_src` would pin down the fallback's correctness too.

**3. Fourth copy site intentionally left as plain `copy_`?**
`routed_experts.py:815` (the `w2` bias path in the expert-bias branch) still
uses `expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)`. I believe that's fine — expert biases
are 1-D/small so the helper's `ndim >= 2` guard would fall straight through —
but worth a one-line comment in the PR description so future readers don't
read it as an oversight.

**4. Datapoint request for the TP>1 row-run path.**
The `stride(-1) == 1` branch (TP-narrowed slabs) still pays a row-run memcpy
on the host; @jadechip's 2.2x B200 datapoint was TP=2, while the per-copy
microbenchmarks are TP=1. A sentence in the PR body on expected gain for
TP>1 (where the row-run branch is the hot path) would set expectations
correctly for operators.

Also confirming the PR applies cleanly on current main: the `_load_w2` inline
block it removes matches main byte-for-byte, and `cdiv` is already imported,
so no rebase obstacles from the last month of main.

Nice work — the generalization to `routed_experts.py` (any transposed fused-MoE
checkpoint, not just Llama-4/ModelOpt) is what makes this the fix #31624
needs, rather than another `.contiguous()` patch.

— Joseph (@JosephYouNew), reviewed on behalf of nothing but my own curiosity;
happy to help test or benchmark follow-ups.

Thanks for preserving the bounded-write path from #54699, and thanks @JosephYouNew for the review. I checked the chunk sizes and source strides on CPU.

The few-row case does exceed 1 MiB per copy, but clamping the chunk count to the row count leaves that unchanged: two 2 MiB rows still produce two 2 MiB copies. A strict byte bound would need tiling within a row, or the description could qualify the bound as row-granular.

For the fallback test, `base.transpose(-1, -2).narrow(1, 0, 16)` still takes the row-run branch: transposing it back leaves `stride(-1) == 1`. A genuinely doubly-strided view such as `base[::2, ::2].T` reaches the gather fallback.

I agree that documenting the 1-D bias exclusion would help. I haven't measured GPU peak memory or TP>1 loading on this revision, so I don't have updated numbers for those yet.
